questions.question: A Mendelian experiment consisted of breeding tall pea plants bearing violet flowers with short pea plants bearing white flowers. The progeny all bore violet flowers, but almost half of them were short. This suggests that the genetic make-up of the tall parent can be depicted as
options: TTWW
TTww
TtWW
TtWw
questions.explanation: All flowers violet → at least one W allele from tall parent. Half progeny short → tall parent is Tt (heterozygous). Tall parent genotype: TtWW.

questions.question: If a trait A exists in 10% of a population of an asexually reproducing species and a trait B exists in 60% of the same population, which trait is likely to have arisen earlier?
options: Trait A, because it is rarer
Trait B, because higher frequency suggests it arose earlier and spread
Both arose at the same time
Cannot be determined without DNA testing
questions.explanation: In asexual reproduction, fewer variations arise. A trait present in more individuals (60%) likely appeared earlier and has been copied more times.

questions.question: How does the creation of variations in a species promote survival?
options: Variations make all individuals identical
Variations ensure some individuals may survive if environment changes
Variations prevent reproduction
Variations only harm the species
questions.explanation: Variation creates diversity so if conditions change, some variants may survive while others may not — species continues.

questions.question: How do Mendel's experiments show that traits may be dominant or recessive?
options: F1 showed both traits equally
F1 showed only dominant trait; recessive reappeared in F2 in 3:1 ratio
Recessive trait always appears in F1
Dominant and recessive traits blend in F1
questions.explanation: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) with pure short (tt) — F1 all tall (dominant). F2 had 3 tall : 1 short — recessive reappeared.

questions.question: How do Mendel's experiments show that traits are inherited independently?
options: All traits are always linked together
Dihybrid cross produced new combinations (tall-wrinkled, short-round) in 9:3:3:1 ratio
Only one trait can be inherited at a time
F1 always matches one parent exactly
questions.explanation: Dihybrid cross of seed shape and colour produced four phenotypes including new combinations — traits assort independently.

questions.question: How is the sex of the child determined in human beings?
options: Mother decides sex by producing X or Y eggs
Father determines sex — X sperm → girl (XX), Y sperm → boy (XY)
Sex is determined by diet during pregnancy
Both parents contribute Y chromosome equally
questions.explanation: Mother always gives X chromosome. Father gives X (girl) or Y (boy). Sex determined by father's sperm.

questions.question: A man with blood group A marries a woman with blood group O and their daughter has blood group O. Can we determine which blood group is dominant?
options: Yes, O is definitely dominant
Yes, A is definitely dominant
No — father could be AO heterozygote, so data is insufficient
Yes, AB is dominant over both
questions.explanation: A can be AA or AO. If father is AO and mother OO, child can be O. Need more data to determine dominance.

questions.question: A tall pea plant could have genotype TT or Tt. What term describes this visible tallness?
options: Genotype
Phenotype
Variation
Mutation
questions.explanation: Phenotype is the observable trait (tall). Genotype is the genetic makeup (TT or Tt).
